get.summary:
Reads every lifecycle event for a contact - create, update, delete, overrides and sign-in
unlocks - newest first.
get.description:
Eventually consistent, on the same terms as M:EdGraph.HttpAggregators.Tenant.Api.Controllers.v1.EnrollmentAdminController.GetEnrollmentContactOverrides(System.String,System.Guid,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken).
`EventType` on `GetAllChangesRequest` is a single optional string, so it cannot express "any of these event types" on its own. The filter is built through `Filter` instead - a raw Elasticsearch `query_string` - while `EntityType` and `EntityId` stay the typed fields M:EdGraph.HttpAggregators.Tenant.Api.Controllers.v1.EnrollmentAdminController.GetEnrollmentContactOverrides(System.String,System.Guid,System.Int32,System.Int32,System.String,System.Threading.CancellationToken) already uses. The change log applies the typed fields as `filter` clauses and `Filter` as a `must` clause on the same bool query, so the two combine as an AND: this call still never leaves this contact's own entity scope.
The event types covered are EdGraph.HttpAggregators.Tenant.Api.Controllers.v1.ViewModels.Responses.EnrollmentAdmin.ContactOverrideHistoryExtensions.ContactEventTypes, which tracks what the Enrollment outbox publishes against a contact.

get.summary: Reads a contact's override history, newest first.
get.description:
Eventually consistent. A change reaches the log through Enrollment's outbox, so an entry can be a few seconds behind a write that has already succeeded. Render the current value from the contact itself and use this for what preceded it.
One route for both details, unlike the writes: this is a single ordered log and each entry names its own detail, so splitting it would mean two requests to render one contact's timeline and two page counts to reconcile.

post.summary: Creates or updates an Enrollment Contact by its source-system `contactId`.
post.description:
Upsert semantics: unique per `contactId`. A first call creates the contact; a later call for the same `contactId` overwrites the SIS-sourced fields where they differ, and no-ops when they are identical. An existing email/phone override is never touched by this call - see the `overrides/emails` and `overrides/phones` routes for that.
`email` and `phone` here are the SIS-sourced values, which is what a contact starts with. Changing either afterwards is an override rather than an update - see the `overrides/emails` and `overrides/phones` routes.

Pathway (the pathway/screen catalog entity) is unrelated to the Registration/Application
rename and is not touched here - only the message name below stays as-is.

rank.description:
The family's preference order within the round. 1-based and contiguous across the
registration - the matcher's contract. Assigned server-side, never supplied by a caller.

priority.description: The priority tier - sibling, staff, feeder, PreK. Unset until the priority engine stamps it.

applicationRoundId.description: Foreign key into the application round this entry was submitted to.

One Program-seat choice on a Registration - zero-to-many, independently approvable. See
ApproveRegistrationApplication / GetRegistrationApplications.

id.description:
The contact entry's id, and the link to the contact roster: submission overwrites whatever
the caller sent with the resolved or auto-created EnrollmentContact document's own id, so
this is the key a join back to that roster goes through.

contactId.description:
The external SIS-side contact code, not the link to the EnrollmentContact document - that is
id (field 1). Registrations written before AB#18541 stored the link here instead; those
values are being nulled, so treat a value in this field as legacy rather than as the link.

progress.description:
Decimal progress (0-100, 2dp) carried as an invariant-culture string,
mirroring the legacy enrollmentresults.proto completedProgress convention.

EnrollmentApi.EnrollmentRegistrations.V1.description:
The linked EnrollmentStudent aggregate. id is that aggregate's own id; studentId is the SIS id;
studentLocalId is the local id - passed through as-is, no aggregator-side logic.
